# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 51 (Bi-Vb Pc51)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc51
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 51
**Title (English, from literature):** Entering a monks’ monastery
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc51
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ārāmapavisana-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 51) governs the entry of nuns into a monks' monastery (*ārāma*) [SuttaCentral; Roth 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun who enters a monks' monastery without obtaining permission commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Roth 1997]. In the traditional background story, nuns entered a monastery while monks were clad in only a single robe; after an initial prohibition, the rule underwent modification to specify that permission must be sought when a monk is present (*santam bhikkhum anāpucchā*) [Roth 1997; Hüsken 1997]. Monastic settlements of monks were typically located outside the village while nuns resided within settlements, creating asymmetric boundaries; while no rule precisely mirrors this for monks, Hüsken notes that Bhikkhu Pācittiya 23 provides a comparable restriction concerning monks visiting the nuns' quarters [Hüsken 1997]. The rule is further commented upon by Buddhaghosa in the Vinaya commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) [Roth 1997].
Curated parallels recorded in SuttaCentral confirm that this rule is shared across the principal Vinaya lineages, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pc 51) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pc 51), the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 144*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 101*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 153*), Mahāsāṃghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 116*), and the Sanskrit Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc116*) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with shared legal formulas in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (notably Pācittiya 85 and 46) and various Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules (such as Pc 85, 94, 84, and 62) [DharmaNexus].
